stem: Local government is the government at the:
options: Village and district level, and at the level of towns and cities (the grassroots level)
solution: Local government is the government at the local level — at the level of villages and small towns (grassroots) — dealing with the everyday problems and needs of ordinary citizens; it is the third tier of government, closest to the people.

stem: The basic idea behind local government is that:
options: Local people can best understand and address their own problems and needs, and their participation in decision-making improves the quality of democracy
solution: The basic idea behind local government is that local people know their own problems and needs best; local decision-making leads to more efficient and responsive solutions, and the direct participation of ordinary people in governance strengthens and deepens democracy at the grassroots.

stem: Local government is important because:
options: It brings democracy closer to the people, enables direct participation, promotes local development, and helps resolve local problems quickly and effectively
solution: Local government is important because it brings decision-making closer to the people (direct participation), makes democracy more meaningful at the grassroots, is well-suited to address local problems and development needs efficiently, and encourages a sense of responsibility and political awareness among citizens.

stem: In rural areas, local government is known as:
solution: In the rural areas, local government is known as Panchayati Raj; it is a system of local self-government for villages, historically rooted in the Indian tradition of village panchayats.

stem: The framers of the Constitution included local self-government among the Directive Principles of State Policy through:
solution: Article 40 of the Directive Principles of State Policy directs the state to take steps to organise village panchayats and endow them with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as units of self-government; however, as a directive principle, it was initially non-binding.

stem: The major weakness of local government in India before 1992 was that:
options: It was not given constitutional status; elections were not held regularly, bodies were often superseded, and they lacked funds and powers, so local government remained weak and ineffective
solution: Before the 1992 amendments, local government suffered because it did not have constitutional status; elections to local bodies were not held regularly, these bodies were frequently dissolved or superseded by the state governments, and they lacked adequate powers, funds and functions — leaving local government weak, dependent and ineffective.

stem: The two landmark amendments that gave constitutional status to local government in India were the:
solution: The 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts, passed in 1992 (came into force in 1993), gave constitutional status to local self-government; the 73rd Amendment deals with rural local government (panchayats) and the 74th Amendment deals with urban local government (municipalities).

stem: The 73rd Amendment deals with rural local bodies (panchayats), while the 74th Amendment deals with:
options: Urban local bodies (municipalities and municipal corporations)
solution: The 73rd Amendment provides for rural local government (Panchayati Raj institutions — panchayats), while the 74th Amendment provides for urban local government (Nagar Palikas — municipalities and municipal corporations) in the towns and cities.

stem: The 73rd Amendment provides for a uniform three-tier structure of Panchayati Raj. The three tiers are the:
solution: The 73rd Amendment provides for a three-tier structure of Panchayati Raj: the Gram Panchayat at the village level, the Panchayat Samiti (or Mandal/Block) at the intermediate (block) level, and the Zila Parishad at the district level. (States with a population below 20 lakh may not have the intermediate tier.)

stem: The Gram Sabha, provided for under the 73rd Amendment, consists of:
options: All the adult members registered as voters in the panchayat area (the whole village electorate)
solution: The Gram Sabha consists of all the adult members registered as voters in the Gram Panchayat area (the entire village electorate); it is meant to be a forum for direct democracy where villagers discuss and oversee the working of the panchayat, approve its plans and budget, and hold it accountable.

stem: Under the 73rd Amendment, it is mandatory to hold elections to the local bodies regularly, and if a local body is dissolved before its term, fresh elections must be held within:
solution: The 73rd Amendment made it mandatory to hold regular elections to local bodies every five years; and if any local body is dissolved before the completion of its five-year term, fresh elections must be held within six months of its dissolution — preventing the earlier practice of prolonged supersession.

stem: The term of every local body (panchayat/municipality) under the 73rd and 74th Amendments is:
solution: The term of every local body (panchayat or municipality) is five years; if the state government dissolves a local body before the end of its term, fresh elections must be conducted within six months.

stem: The 73rd and 74th Amendments provide for the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in local bodies in proportion to their:
solution: The 73rd and 74th Amendments provide for the reservation of seats for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the local bodies (and in the offices of chairpersons) in proportion to their population in the concerned local area, ensuring their representation in grassroots governance.

stem: A significant provision of the 73rd and 74th Amendments regarding women is that:
options: One-third of the seats (and offices of chairpersons) in all local bodies are reserved for women
Half the seats are reserved for women
solution: One of the most significant provisions is that one-third of the total seats in all local bodies (panchayats and municipalities), and one-third of the offices of chairpersons at all levels, are reserved for women; this has brought a large number of women into grassroots politics and decision-making. (Many states have since raised this to 50%.)

stem: The number of women elected to local government bodies as a result of the reservation is estimated to be over:
solution: As a result of the one-third reservation, more than 10 lakh (a million) women have been elected as representatives in the local bodies across the country; this is regarded as one of the largest experiments in bringing women into public decision-making anywhere in the world.

stem: The body created in each state to conduct elections to the local government bodies is the:
solution: The 73rd and 74th Amendments provide for the creation of a State Election Commission in each state, an independent body responsible for conducting elections to the panchayats and municipalities; this ensures that local elections are held regularly and fairly, independent of the state government's control.

stem: The body created to review the financial position of local bodies and recommend the distribution of funds between the state and local governments is the:
solution: The 73rd and 74th Amendments provide for the creation of a State Finance Commission in each state, appointed every five years, to review the financial position of the local bodies and to recommend the distribution of financial resources (taxes, duties, grants) between the state and local governments — an important step towards the financial empowerment of local bodies.

stem: The subjects that state legislatures can devolve to the panchayats and municipalities are listed in which schedules added by the 73rd and 74th Amendments?
options: The Eleventh Schedule (for panchayats) and the Twelfth Schedule (for municipalities)
solution: The 73rd Amendment added the Eleventh Schedule, listing 29 subjects (functions) that can be transferred to the panchayats; the 74th Amendment added the Twelfth Schedule, listing 18 subjects that can be transferred to the municipalities. The actual devolution of these functions, funds and functionaries is left to the state legislatures.

stem: A limitation of the local government reforms is that the actual transfer of powers, functions and finances to local bodies depends on the:
options: State governments, which have often been reluctant to devolve real powers, funds and functionaries to the local bodies
solution: A major limitation is that while the Constitution provides the framework, the actual devolution of powers, functions, funds, and functionaries to the local bodies is left to the discretion of the state governments; many states have been reluctant to transfer real powers and adequate finances, leaving local bodies dependent and their autonomy limited in practice.

stem: The provision that all three levels of the panchayat are directly or indirectly elected has ensured that:
options: Local government is genuinely representative and accountable to the local people through regular elections
solution: The provision for the election of members at all levels of the panchayat (Gram Panchayat members are directly elected; higher tiers are constituted through election) ensures that local government is genuinely representative and democratically accountable to the local people, who can choose and change their representatives through regular five-yearly elections.

stem: For urban areas, the 74th Amendment provides for three types of urban local bodies. A 'Nagar Panchayat' is for a:
options: Transitional area (an area in transition from rural to urban)
solution: The 74th Amendment provides for three types of urban local bodies based on the size of the urban area: a Nagar Panchayat for a transitional area (an area in transition from rural to urban); a Municipal Council (Municipality) for a smaller urban area (town); and a Municipal Corporation for a larger urban area (a big city).

stem: The political head of a Municipal Corporation is called the:
solution: The political head of a Municipal Corporation is the Mayor; the Municipal Corporation administers a large city. (In a Gram Panchayat the head is the Sarpanch, and in a Municipality/Municipal Council the head is the Chairperson/President.)

stem: The 74th Amendment also provides for the constitution of 'Ward Committees' in municipalities to:
options: Bring administration closer to the people at the ward level and enable greater public participation in cities
solution: The 74th Amendment provides for the constitution of Ward Committees within municipalities (especially those with a population of three lakh or more), consisting of one or more wards; these committees are meant to bring the municipal administration closer to the people at the ward level and enable greater public participation in the governance of larger cities.

stem: The experience of the state of Kerala with the 'People's Planning Campaign' is cited as an example of:
options: The successful devolution of powers and funds to local bodies and effective grassroots participatory planning
solution: Kerala's 'People's Planning Campaign' (Kudumbashree and the People's Plan) is cited as a successful example of genuine decentralisation, where substantial powers and funds were devolved to local bodies, and local people actively participated in planning and implementing development schemes; it demonstrates the potential of local self-government when powers and resources are truly transferred.

stem: The extension of the provisions of the 73rd Amendment to the tribal/scheduled areas is provided through a special law known as:
options: PESA (the Panchayats Extension to Scheduled Areas Act, 1996)
solution: The provisions of the 73rd Amendment (Panchayati Raj) were extended to the tribal-dominated Scheduled (Fifth Schedule) areas through the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996, commonly known as PESA; it gives special powers to the Gram Sabhas in these areas to protect the traditions, customs, resources (especially minor forest produce and land), and self-governance of tribal communities.

stem: Which of the following is a positive achievement of the 73rd and 74th Amendments?
options: The regularisation of local elections, the entry of a large number of women and members of SC/ST communities into local governance, and the deepening of democracy at the grassroots
solution: Positive achievements of the 73rd and 74th Amendments include: making local elections regular and constitutionally mandatory; bringing over a million women and large numbers of SC/ST representatives into local decision-making through reservation; empowering marginalised sections; and generally deepening and strengthening democracy at the grassroots level, giving ordinary citizens a direct stake in governance.

stem: A criticism of the working of local government is that even though women get elected, sometimes:
options: Real power is exercised by their male relatives (the phenomenon of 'sarpanch pati'), which undermines the spirit of women's empowerment
solution: A criticism of local government's working is that in some places, even though women are elected (due to reservation), the real decision-making power is often exercised by their male relatives (husbands, fathers) — a phenomenon sometimes called 'sarpanch pati' — which undermines the goal of genuine women's empowerment; however, over time, many women representatives have gained confidence and become effective leaders in their own right.

stem: The devolution of '3 Fs' is considered essential for making local government effective. These 3 Fs are:
solution: For local government to be truly effective and autonomous, the '3 Fs' must be devolved to them: Functions (clear responsibilities and powers), Funds (adequate financial resources), and Functionaries (staff/personnel to carry out the work). Without the genuine transfer of all three from the state governments, local bodies remain weak and dependent.

stem: The historical significance of Panchayati Raj in the Indian tradition, and Mahatma Gandhi's vision of 'Gram Swaraj', was that:
options: Villages should be self-reliant, self-governing units and the foundation of Indian democracy; power should be decentralised to the grassroots
solution: Mahatma Gandhi strongly advocated the decentralisation of power to the villages; his vision of 'Gram Swaraj' held that villages should be self-reliant, self-governing units and the foundation of Indian democracy, with power flowing upwards from the grassroots. The Panchayati Raj system draws inspiration from this vision of decentralised, participatory village democracy.

stem: The three-tier Panchayati Raj system was first recommended by which committee, leading to its early (pre-1992) introduction in states like Rajasthan and Andhra Pradesh?
solution: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) recommended the establishment of a three-tier Panchayati Raj system; on its recommendation, Rajasthan (in 1959) became the first state to introduce Panchayati Raj, followed by Andhra Pradesh. (The later Ashok Mehta Committee also reviewed the system, and the 73rd Amendment finally gave it constitutional status in 1992.)

stem: The main reason local government strengthens democracy is that:
options: It enables the direct participation of ordinary citizens in governance, makes government more responsive and accountable at the grassroots, and creates a large body of grassroots political leaders
solution: Local government strengthens democracy because it enables the direct and widespread participation of ordinary citizens (including women, SCs, STs) in decision-making; it makes government more responsive and accountable at the grassroots level (where problems are best understood); and it creates a vast body of grassroots-level political leaders, thereby deepening and broadening the base of democracy.

stem: Which of the following statements about the Gram Sabha is correct?
options: It is an elected body of a few members
It is a body of all adult voters of the village that can hold the Gram Panchayat accountable, and is a forum for direct democracy
It is appointed by the state government
It has no role in the panchayat
solution: The Gram Sabha is not an elected body of a few members but the general body of all the adult voters (electorate) of the village; it is meant to be a forum for direct democracy, where villagers can review the panchayat's functioning, approve its budget and plans, and hold their elected representatives directly accountable, thereby ensuring transparency and participation.

stem: The reservation of offices of chairpersons (like sarpanch, mayor) for SCs, STs and women, in addition to the reservation of ordinary seats, is important because:
options: It ensures that marginalised groups and women not only enter local bodies but also occupy positions of leadership and real decision-making authority
solution: The reservation of the offices of chairpersons (heads of local bodies) — in addition to ordinary seats — for SCs, STs, and women is important because it ensures that these marginalised groups and women occupy positions of actual leadership and decision-making authority, not just ordinary membership; this gives them real power and a stronger voice in local governance.

stem: The idea that local governments should be given greater financial autonomy is important because:
options: Without adequate and independent financial resources, local bodies cannot effectively perform their functions and remain dependent on the state governments
Finances should be controlled only by the centre
solution: Greater financial autonomy for local governments is important because without adequate and reliable financial resources (their own sources of revenue plus assured transfers), local bodies cannot effectively carry out the functions assigned to them and remain heavily dependent on the discretion and grants of the state governments; genuine decentralisation requires the devolution of adequate funds along with functions.

stem: The 73rd and 74th Amendments represent a major step in Indian democracy because they:
options: Created and constitutionally protected a third tier of government, making decentralisation and grassroots democracy a permanent feature of the Indian political system
Centralised all power at the centre
solution: The 73rd and 74th Amendments represent a major step because they created a constitutionally protected third tier of government (rural and urban local bodies), making decentralisation and grassroots democracy a permanent and mandatory feature of the Indian political system; they ensured regular elections, reservations for weaker sections and women, and the framework for devolution — thereby institutionalising and deepening democracy at the local level.

stem: A key difference between local government before and after the 1992 amendments is that:
options: Before 1992, local bodies lacked constitutional status, regular elections, and were often superseded; after 1992, they have constitutional status, mandatory regular elections, reservations, and defined structures
solution: The key difference is that before 1992, local government had no constitutional status; elections were irregular, bodies were frequently dissolved/superseded, and they lacked defined powers and finances. After the 73rd and 74th Amendments (1992), local bodies gained constitutional status, mandatory regular five-yearly elections (with a State Election Commission), reservations for SCs/STs and women, a uniform structure, and provisions for financial support (State Finance Commission), transforming them into genuine institutions of self-government.

stem: Which of the following correctly lists the three tiers of rural local government from the lowest to the highest level?
options: Zila Parishad, Panchayat Samiti, Gram Panchayat
Gram Panchayat (village), Panchayat Samiti/Block (intermediate), Zila Parishad (district)
solution: The three tiers of rural local government (Panchayati Raj), from the lowest to the highest, are: the Gram Panchayat at the village level; the Panchayat Samiti (also called Block/Mandal/Taluka Panchayat) at the intermediate (block) level; and the Zila Parishad at the district level.

stem: The role of the State Election Commission in local government is significant because:
options: It ensures that local elections are conducted regularly, freely and fairly, independent of the state government, preventing the earlier practice of postponing local elections indefinitely
solution: The State Election Commission is significant because it is an independent constitutional authority responsible for conducting local body elections regularly, freely and fairly; its independence from the state government prevents the earlier practice where state governments would indefinitely postpone or avoid holding local elections, thereby ensuring that local self-government remains genuinely democratic and regularly renewed.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'Local Governments' is that:
options: Local self-government (Panchayati Raj and municipalities), given constitutional status by the 73rd and 74th Amendments, is the third tier of Indian democracy that deepens participation and empowers marginalised sections, though its effectiveness depends on the genuine devolution of powers, funds and functionaries by the states
solution: The chapter concludes that local self-government — rural (Panchayati Raj) and urban (municipalities) — is a vital third tier of Indian democracy, given constitutional status and permanence by the 73rd and 74th Amendments (1992). These reforms have deepened democracy at the grassroots by ensuring regular elections, reservations for women and weaker sections (bringing millions into governance), and defined structures. However, the true effectiveness and autonomy of local government depends on the genuine devolution of the '3 Fs' (functions, funds, and functionaries) by the state governments, which remains a work in progress.

stem: The 73rd Amendment provides that the intermediate tier (Panchayat Samiti) may not be constituted in states having a population not exceeding:
solution: The 73rd Amendment provides for a three-tier structure, but states having a population not exceeding twenty lakh (2 million) are given the option of not constituting the intermediate (Panchayat Samiti) tier; smaller states may thus have only a two-tier system.

stem: The head of a Gram Panchayat, who is the elected leader of the village council, is called the:
solution: The head of a Gram Panchayat is called the Sarpanch (also known as Pradhan or President in some states); the Sarpanch is the elected leader of the village-level council (the panch and sarpanch together form the Gram Panchayat), presiding over its meetings and coordinating its work.

stem: The Ashok Mehta Committee (1977) recommended a change to a two-tier Panchayati Raj system. Which two tiers did it recommend?
options: Mandal Panchayat (at the level of a group of villages) and Zila Parishad
solution: The Ashok Mehta Committee (1977) reviewed the working of Panchayati Raj and recommended a two-tier system, consisting of the Mandal Panchayat (at the level of a group of villages) and the Zila Parishad (at the district level); it also emphasised the district as the key unit for planning and development, and greater political and financial powers for local bodies.

stem: Which of the following is one of the functions typically performed by a Gram Panchayat?
options: Providing local amenities such as water supply, sanitation, street lighting, local roads, and maintaining records; implementing development and welfare schemes
solution: A Gram Panchayat typically performs functions such as: providing basic local amenities (drinking water supply, sanitation, drainage, street lighting, construction and maintenance of village roads); maintaining public records (like births and deaths); and implementing various development, welfare, and poverty-alleviation schemes at the village level.

stem: The provision that reservations for women and SC/ST chairperson positions should rotate among different constituencies over successive elections is meant to:
options: Ensure that the benefit of reservation is spread across different areas and that different constituencies get the opportunity to have reserved and unreserved seats over time
solution: The rotation of reserved seats and chairperson positions among different constituencies over successive elections ensures that the benefit of reservation is distributed across different areas over time, and that no single constituency is permanently reserved or permanently unreserved; this spreads representation and opportunity more equitably among various localities.

stem: Some states have gone beyond the constitutional minimum by increasing the reservation for women in local bodies to:
solution: While the Constitution mandates a minimum of one-third reservation for women in local bodies, many states (such as Bihar, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, and others) have gone further and increased the reservation for women to 50 per cent (half the seats), reflecting a growing commitment to women's political empowerment at the grassroots.

stem: The primary reason why decentralisation to local government is considered valuable is that a large number of problems and issues are:
options: Best decided at the national level
Best settled at the local level, where people have a better understanding of the problems and a direct stake in solving them
solution: Decentralisation to local government is valuable because a large number of problems and issues (relating to local development, amenities, and welfare) are best settled at the local level, where the people directly affected have a better understanding of the ground realities, know their priorities, and have a direct stake in finding effective and appropriate solutions.

stem: A challenge faced by local governments is that, in many cases, they have been given responsibilities without:
options: Adequate financial resources and independent sources of revenue to fulfil those responsibilities
solution: A major challenge for local governments is that they are often assigned a range of functions and responsibilities but are not given adequate financial resources and independent sources of revenue to carry them out; this mismatch between responsibilities and resources leaves local bodies dependent on the state governments and hampers their effective functioning.

stem: The urban local body responsible for administering a small town or a smaller urban area (as distinct from a big city) is the:
solution: The Municipal Council (also simply called a Municipality) is the urban local body that administers a smaller urban area or a town; a larger city is administered by a Municipal Corporation, and a transitional (rural-to-urban) area is administered by a Nagar Panchayat.

stem: The reservation of one-third of seats for women in local bodies is significant for Indian democracy because:
options: It has brought large numbers of women into active political life and decision-making for the first time, empowering them and making local governance more inclusive
solution: The one-third reservation for women is significant because it has brought over a million women into active political life and grassroots decision-making, many for the first time; it has empowered women, given them a formal voice in local governance, challenged traditional gender roles, and made local government more inclusive and representative of half the population.

stem: The two landmark amendments that gave constitutional status to local governments were passed in the year:
solution: The 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments, passed in 1992 and coming into force in 1993, gave constitutional status to rural and urban local governments respectively.

stem: The 73rd Amendment deals with __________ local bodies.
solution: The 73rd Amendment deals with rural local government (Panchayati Raj institutions), while the 74th Amendment deals with urban local bodies (municipalities).

stem: The 74th Amendment deals with __________ local bodies.
solution: The 74th Amendment provides for urban local governments — municipalities, municipal corporations and nagar panchayats — giving them constitutional status.

stem: The 73rd Amendment provides for a uniform three-tier structure of panchayats at the village, intermediate (block) and __________ levels.
solution: The 73rd Amendment provides for a three-tier structure of Panchayati Raj at the village (Gram Panchayat), intermediate (Panchayat Samiti/Block), and district (Zila Parishad) levels.

stem: The Gram Sabha, under the 73rd Amendment, consists of:
options: All the adult members (voters) registered in the village panchayat
solution: The Gram Sabha consists of all the adult voters registered within the area of a Gram Panchayat; it is meant to oversee the work of the panchayat and approve its plans and budget.

stem: Under the 73rd and 74th Amendments, at least what fraction of seats in local bodies is reserved for women?
solution: At least one-third of the total seats in panchayats and municipalities (and one-third of the chairperson positions) are reserved for women, including women of SC and ST communities.

stem: The term of every local body (panchayat or municipality) under the amendments is fixed at:
solution: The term of every panchayat and municipality is fixed at five years; if a local body is dissolved before its term, fresh elections must be held within six months.

stem: If a local body is dissolved before its term, fresh elections must be held within:
solution: To prevent local bodies from being left without elected representatives, the Constitution mandates that elections be held within six months if a panchayat or municipality is dissolved before completing its term.

stem: The independent body created in each state to conduct elections to the local bodies is the:
solution: The 73rd and 74th Amendments require each state to set up a State Election Commission to conduct free and fair elections to the panchayats and municipalities.

stem: The body created to review the financial position of local bodies and recommend the sharing of resources is the:
solution: The State Finance Commission is set up every five years to review the financial position of the local bodies and recommend how revenues should be shared between the state and the local governments.

stem: Assertion (A): Local governments were given constitutional status in 1992. Reason (R): Before 1992, local bodies were weak, irregularly elected and dependent on the will of state governments.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
solution: Local governments were given constitutional status because, before 1992, they were weak, elections were not held regularly, and they depended entirely on the state governments' discretion — R explains A.

stem: Assertion (A): Reservation for women in local bodies has increased women's participation in governance. Reason (R): The amendments reserve one-third of seats and chairperson posts for women.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
solution: The mandatory reservation of one-third of seats and offices for women has brought a large number of women into local governance — R explains A.

stem: The number of elected representatives in India's local bodies after the amendments is about:
solution: The 73rd and 74th Amendments created about 32-36 lakh (over 3 million) elected local representatives, the largest number of elected representatives anywhere in the world.

stem: The three-tier Panchayati Raj system was first recommended in India by the:
solution: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) first recommended the establishment of a three-tier Panchayati Raj system, which was implemented in states like Rajasthan and Andhra Pradesh in the late 1950s.

stem: The Ashok Mehta Committee (1977) recommended a change to a __________ system of local government.
solution: The Ashok Mehta Committee (1977) recommended a two-tier Panchayati Raj system (Zila Parishad at the district level and Mandal Panchayat below it), and greater powers for local bodies.

stem: The head of a Gram Panchayat, the elected leader of the village body, is usually called the:
solution: The Gram Panchayat is headed by an elected president, usually called the Sarpanch (or Pradhan/Adhyaksh in different states), assisted by elected members called Panch.

stem: The urban local body responsible for administering a small town in transition from rural to urban is the:
solution: The 74th Amendment provides for three types of urban bodies: Nagar Panchayats for areas in transition from rural to urban, Municipal Councils for smaller towns, and Municipal Corporations for larger cities.

stem: The 74th Amendment provides for the constitution of 'Ward Committees' in order to:
options: Bring administration closer to the people at the neighbourhood level
solution: The 74th Amendment provides for the constitution of Ward Committees within municipalities to ensure people's participation and bring urban governance closer to the residents at the ward/neighbourhood level.

stem: The subjects that state legislatures may devolve to the panchayats are listed in the:
solution: The Eleventh Schedule (added by the 73rd Amendment) lists 29 subjects, such as agriculture, education, health and water, that state legislatures may devolve to the panchayats.

stem: The subjects that may be devolved to urban local bodies (municipalities) are listed in the:
solution: The Twelfth Schedule (added by the 74th Amendment) lists 18 subjects, such as urban planning, water supply and public health, that may be devolved to the municipalities.

stem: The state of Kerala is well known for its experiment in decentralised planning called the:
solution: Kerala's 'People's Plan Campaign' devolved substantial funds and planning powers to local bodies, involving people directly in preparing and implementing local development plans — a notable success of decentralisation.

stem: The extension of the provisions of the 73rd Amendment to the tribal (Scheduled) areas is done through the:
options: PESA Act (Panchayats Extension to Scheduled Areas Act, 1996)
solution: The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 (PESA) extended the provisions of Part IX (73rd Amendment) to the Scheduled Areas, giving tribal Gram Sabhas special powers over local resources.

stem: The devolution of the '3 Fs' considered essential for effective local government refers to:
solution: For local governments to work effectively, they need the devolution of the '3 Fs' — Funds (financial resources), Functions (powers and subjects), and Functionaries (staff) — from the state governments.

stem: A limitation of the local government reforms is that:
options: State governments have often not devolved adequate funds, functions and functionaries
Local bodies have too much power
solution: A key limitation is that although elections are held regularly, many state governments have been reluctant to transfer adequate funds, functions and functionaries to the local bodies, limiting their effectiveness.

stem: Match the local body with its area: (i) Gram Panchayat (ii) Municipal Corporation (iii) Zila Parishad — (a) big city (b) village (c) district:
solution: The Gram Panchayat governs a village, the Municipal Corporation a big city, and the Zila Parishad a district.

stem: The reservation of offices of chairpersons (sarpanch, mayor) for women and SC/ST is significant because it:
options: Ensures these groups reach leadership positions in local government
solution: Reservation of chairperson positions ensures that women and members of Scheduled Castes and Tribes not only get seats but also occupy leadership offices in local governance, deepening their participation and empowerment.

stem: The three tiers of rural local government (Panchayati Raj) are the Gram Panchayat, the Panchayat Samiti (Block) and the:
solution: The three tiers of Panchayati Raj are the Gram Panchayat at the village level, the Panchayat Samiti (Block/Mandal) at the intermediate level, and the Zila Parishad at the district level.

stem: The role of the State Election Commission in local government is to:
options: Conduct free and fair elections to panchayats and municipalities regularly
solution: The State Election Commission is responsible for the superintendence, direction and control of the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of all elections to the panchayats and municipalities.

stem: The 73rd Amendment made it mandatory to hold elections to local bodies:
solution: A major achievement of the 73rd Amendment is that it made it constitutionally mandatory to hold regular elections to local bodies every five years, ending the earlier practice of arbitrary postponement by states.

stem: The reservation of one-third of seats for women in local bodies has led to:
options: More than a million women becoming elected representatives
solution: The reservation has brought over a million women into elected local government positions, giving women unprecedented representation and a role in grassroots decision-making.

stem: A challenge faced by local governments is that:
options: They often depend heavily on state grants and lack adequate financial resources
solution: Local governments often lack their own adequate sources of revenue and depend heavily on grants from the state and central governments, which limits their financial autonomy and effectiveness.

stem: The reason decentralisation to local government strengthens democracy is that it:
options: Brings governance closer to the people and enables direct participation
solution: Decentralisation strengthens democracy by bringing the government closer to the people, allowing ordinary citizens to participate directly in decisions affecting their lives, and deepening democratic culture at the grassroots.

stem: The historical significance of Panchayati Raj in the Indian tradition is that:
options: Village panchayats (self-governing village councils) have existed since ancient times
solution: Local self-government through village panchayats has deep roots in the Indian tradition; the idea of self-governing village communities is ancient, and Gandhi advocated 'Gram Swaraj' (village self-rule).

stem: Gandhi's idea of decentralised governance emphasised making the __________ the basic unit of self-government.
solution: Gandhi advocated 'Gram Swaraj' — making the self-reliant village panchayat the basic unit of Indian democracy and self-government, an idea reflected in the later strengthening of Panchayati Raj.

stem: The framers of the Constitution originally placed local self-government in the:
solution: Originally, local self-government was mentioned only in the Directive Principles (Article 40), which directed the state to organise village panchayats; it was made a constitutional obligation only by the 73rd Amendment.

stem: The 73rd and 74th Amendments represent a major step in India's:
options: Democratic decentralisation and deepening of democracy
solution: The 73rd and 74th Amendments are a landmark in democratic decentralisation, empowering local self-government and deepening democracy by involving people directly in governance at the grassroots level.

stem: A key difference between local government before and after the 1992 amendments is that after 1992:
options: Elections became regular and mandatory, and local bodies got constitutional status
solution: Before 1992 local bodies were weak and elections irregular; after 1992 they gained constitutional status, regular mandatory elections, reservation for women and weaker sections, and independent election and finance commissions.

stem: The idea of local self-government is rooted in the democratic principle of:
options: People governing themselves at the level closest to them
solution: Local self-government embodies the democratic principle that people should govern themselves at the level closest to their daily lives, enabling meaningful participation and accountability.

stem: The devolution of powers to local bodies varies across states because:
options: The extent of devolution is left to the state legislatures
solution: While the amendments provide a common framework, the actual devolution of the 29 subjects (Eleventh Schedule) and 18 subjects (Twelfth Schedule) is left to the state legislatures, so the degree of empowerment varies across states.

stem: The provision that all three levels of the panchayat are directly elected (in most states) ensures:
options: Greater democratic accountability at each tier
solution: Direct or indirect election of members at each tier of the panchayat system ensures that representatives are accountable to the people, strengthening democracy at the local level.

stem: The main reason local government strengthens democracy is that it:
options: Creates opportunities for ordinary citizens, including women and the marginalised, to participate in governance
solution: Local government strengthens democracy by creating institutions and opportunities for ordinary people — including women, SCs, STs and the poor — to participate in decision-making and hold their representatives accountable.

stem: A criticism of the working of local government is that even after the amendments:
options: Many state governments have not fully empowered the local bodies
solution: A common criticism is that despite constitutional status, many state governments have not transferred adequate powers, funds and functionaries, leaving local bodies dependent and under-empowered in practice.

stem: Local government is important because it:
options: Handles local issues efficiently and promotes participatory democracy
solution: Local government is important because it efficiently addresses local problems, brings decision-making close to the people, promotes participatory democracy, and helps in the development of the area.

stem: The idea of local self-government is rooted in the democratic principle that:
options: Power should be concentrated at the top
Power and decision-making should be brought as close to the people as possible, enabling their direct participation in matters that affect their daily lives
solution: The idea of local self-government is rooted in the democratic principle that power and decision-making should be brought as close to the people as possible; by enabling the direct participation of ordinary citizens in the governance of matters that affect their everyday lives, local self-government makes democracy more genuine, participatory, responsive, and meaningful at the grassroots level.
